description: Executable judgment corpus for computeArbitration/evaluateCoverage (src/review/reviewCore.js, src/review/coveragePolicy.js). Unlike evaluation-matrix.json in this same directory -- which only checks that a fixed list of case IDs/expected strings is present, and never calls the arbiter -- every case here is fed through the real arbitration functions by tests/unit/reviewArbitrationJudgment.test.ts and asserted against `intendedVerdict`. These cases exercise judgment (severity weighing, coverage quorum, scope containment), not infra/failure-handling, which the existing 12-case matrix already covers well.

cases.description: One persona reports a credible P0; the other four report nothing.
cases.justification: The arbiter is not a vote count across persona opinions -- it aggregates findings by severity across the whole panel. A single credible P0 blocks regardless of how many other personas found nothing, because volume of agreement never substitutes for the presence of a critical defect.

findings.title: Admin endpoint has no auth check
findings.body: The new /admin/users route registered here returns the full user table with no authentication or authorization check, and is wired directly into the public router by this diff.

cases.description: Five personas each raise one P2 nit (reaching the nit-volume threshold on its own), and one of them also raises a P0.
cases.justification: p2Count alone (5, at this panel's fixP2 floor of max(5, panelSize)) would already be enough to trigger FIX_FIRST by nit volume. The P0 must still win outright: candidateVerdict is decided by an if/else-if chain that checks p0Count before it ever looks at p1Count or p2Count, so no quantity of low-severity findings can out-vote one critical one.

cases.description: Only a couple of minor P2 nits are raised across the whole panel; nothing else.
cases.justification: Real but minor findings, well below the nit-volume floor (fixP2 = max(5, panelSize) = 5 for this panel), must not block a release. Blocking on nits alone would make every trivial style comment a merge blocker, which defeats the purpose of severity tiers.

cases.description: A persona reports a real P0 in a file the pull request never touched, alongside a real P1 that IS in the diff.
cases.justification: A genuine defect outside the changed files is not evidence the panel can act on for THIS pull request -- sanitizeFinding drops any finding whose path is not among changedFiles (or whose line falls outside the file's changed hunks) before arbitration ever sees it. The out-of-scope P0 must not surface at all, let alone force a BLOCK; only the in-scope P1 should count.

findings.title: Missing null check on added_line
findings.body: added_line() can receive a null argument from the caller introduced in this diff and will throw.

findings.title: SQL built via string concatenation
findings.body: This existing function concatenates user input directly into a SQL query, which is exploitable, but this file is not part of the current diff and was not changed by it.

cases.description: A single-reviewer panel raises two distinct P1 findings, one below the blocking floor.
cases.justification: blockP1 = max(3, ceil(panelSize / 2)); for a 1-persona panel that floor is 3. Two distinct, real P1 findings is the borderline case a reasonable reviewer could plausibly want to block on -- but the policy's explicit floor says otherwise, so this pins FIX_FIRST rather than letting the boundary drift.

findings.title: Off-by-one in pagination cursor
findings.body: The cursor comparison uses <= where it should use <, returning one duplicate row per page.

findings.title: Unbounded retry loop on network failure
findings.body: This retry has no backoff or cap and will spin indefinitely on a persistent failure.

cases.description: The same single-reviewer panel, but with a third distinct P1 finding added, reaching the blocking floor.
cases.justification: Pins the other side of the same boundary: at blockP1 = 3, the verdict flips to BLOCK. Tested together with p1-floor-boundary-one-below so the floor's exact position cannot silently drift without failing both.

cases.description: 5-persona roster under the default two_thirds quorum (requiredCoverageCount(5, 'two_thirds') === 4); exactly 4 lanes are trustworthy, zero findings.
cases.justification: Pins Finding 1 of the verdict-arbiter review directly in the judgment corpus: the configured coverage quorum is genuinely met here (coverageQuorumSatisfied: true, status: PARTIAL_REVIEW), but mergeEligible/verdict are gated on full coverage only, by design -- see src/review/reviewCore.js and src/review/coveragePolicy.js for the full trace and the incidents (API-2902 and others) that motivate always failing closed on less than the full panel.

cases.description: The same 5-persona roster and policy, but with only 3 trustworthy lanes -- one below the required quorum of 4.
cases.justification: Below the configured quorum, coverage degrades further to 'incomplete' (status: INCOMPLETE_REVIEW, coverageQuorumSatisfied: false) instead of 'partial'. verdict and mergeEligible are identical to the exactly-at case: BLOCK / false either way. The quorum setting changes only the label, never the outcome -- see quorum-boundary-exactly-at-two-thirds.

cases.description: Three of five personas independently describe the same real session-fixation defect, in their own words, at the same file/line. The other two are clean.
cases.justification: Product policy (this review, Decision 2): the same defect found by three lanes must not count three times toward a blocking threshold -- one real P1 should read as one P1. blockP1 for this 5-persona panel is 3. Before computeArbitration clustered near-duplicate claims (claimSimilarity.compareClaims), the un-deduplicated count (p1Count = 3) reached the floor and blocked; now the three findings collapse into one cluster (pairwise similarity 0.575-0.668, all above STRONG_DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD, so they merge regardless of the 10-line window) and p1Count = 1, which only warrants FIX_FIRST. This case used to live in a `knownGapCases` array, run via vitest's `it.fails`, documenting exactly this gap without asserting the broken behavior as correct; it is promoted here now that the fix landed. See src/review/reviewCore.js's clusterFindingsForVerdict for the full trace, calibration notes, and why corroboration (3 lanes agreeing) intentionally has no effect on severity.

findings.title: rotateCredential never calls revokeSessions
findings.body: rotateCredential updates the password hash but never calls revokeSessions, so old session tokens issued before rotateCredential ran stay valid after the password change.

findings.title: revokeSessions is not called by rotateCredential
findings.body: After rotateCredential runs, old session tokens remain valid because rotateCredential never calls revokeSessions for the previous session tokens.

findings.title: Session tokens survive rotateCredential since revokeSessions is not called
findings.body: rotateCredential changes the password but old session tokens survive because revokeSessions is never called by rotateCredential after the password change.
